Jonas — added a few technical clarifications after reviewing the attachments.

1) SCIM provisioning
- We support RFC7643 attribute set and group membership sync. The sample config includes mapping for: userName -> email, name.familyName, name.givenName, externalId.
- Groups are mapped to Redwood roles via the "groupsToRoles" mapping; we use delta sync for large orgs to reduce churn.

2) MFA enforcement and evidence
- MFA is enforced at the IdP for SSO flows (we integrate with SAML/OIDC IdPs). For native login we require TOTP + backup code options for admin roles.
- Attached is a screenshot showing an admin session with a 2FA enforcement banner and an audit extract (redacted) of the 2FA enrollment event.
- Raw auth events are available but will be redacted before sharing. We can produce a CSV extract of auth events between requested dates.

3) Least privilege & service accounts
- Service accounts are scoped to a project and assigned a service_role which has limited API scopes. We maintain an internal expiry and rotation policy for keys; exceptions are tracked in IDM-412 (link in the thread metadata).

Attachment: mfa_enforcement_screenshot.png (image/png)

If you want a short video demo of the SCIM provisioning run, I can schedule 20 minutes with the customer success engineer.

—
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — solid attachments. A couple of security notes to include in the package we share with FinSecure: 

- RBAC exceptions: our temporary elevation process requires a JIRA approval (IDM-412), automated expiry (max 72h), and an audit log entry. We should include a sanitized example ticket and the policy doc excerpt.
- Data minimization: redact admin usernames and user emails when sharing logs; use hashed identifiers where possible.
- Compliance note: mention that dedicated deployments can enable customer-managed KMS which we document in our "Private Deployment — Key Management" section (we'll link the doc).

I'll prepare a short paragraph describing the exception controls and add the policy excerpt to Drive.

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
